title: Structural load and beam sizing calculations
problem: Civil engineers spend hours manually calculating dead loads, live loads, wind loads, and seismic forces per ASCE 7, then sizing beams and columns per ACI 318 or AISC standards. Errors in these calculations can lead to structural failures, stop-work orders, and personal liability for the PE who stamped the documents.
who: Project Engineers and Senior Engineers (PE) doing structural design

skill_spec.name: Structural Load Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates combined design loads (dead, live, wind, snow, seismic) per ASCE 7 load combinations and checks beam/column capacity
skill_spec.formula_hint: ASCE 7-22 load combos: 1.4D, 1.2D+1.6L, 1.2D+1.0W+L, etc. Apply importance factors by risk category. Return governing combo.

example_queries: Calculate the governing load combination for a floor with 20 psf dead load, 50 psf live load, and 30 psf ground snow load, Risk Category II
What is the total factored load on a beam with 400 sq ft tributary area, 25 psf dead load and 100 psf live load?

title: Cut and fill earthwork volume estimation
problem: Calculating earthwork quantities for grading projects requires computing cut and fill volumes from cross-sections or contour data. Engineers often do this manually or in spreadsheets before feeding into Civil 3D, leading to errors in bid estimates that cause cost overruns of tens of thousands of dollars on mid-size projects.
who: Site development and transportation engineers preparing grading plans and cost estimates

skill_spec.name: Cut and Fill Earthwork Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Estimates cut/fill volumes using average end area method from station cross-section data, with shrink/swell factors

inputs.name: cut_areas
inputs.label: Cut cross-section areas (sq ft) at each station

inputs.name: fill_areas
inputs.label: Fill cross-section areas (sq ft) at each station

skill_spec.formula_hint: Average end area: V = (A1+A2)/2 * L / 27 (convert cu ft to cu yd). Apply shrink/swell to adjust compacted fill needs.

example_queries: I have 5 stations at 100 ft intervals with cut areas of 120, 200, 180, 90, 40 sq ft. What's the total cut volume?
Estimate earthwork cost for 5,000 CY of cut and 3,200 CY of fill with $12/CY haul cost and 1.25 shrink factor

title: Stormwater detention pond sizing
problem: Engineers must size stormwater detention/retention basins to meet local and EPA NPDES requirements. This involves calculating pre- and post-development runoff using the Rational Method or SCS/NRCS method, then determining required storage volume. Undersizing means permit denial or flooding; oversizing wastes land and money.
who: Site civil engineers and stormwater designers working on land development projects

skill_spec.name: Stormwater Detention Pond Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Sizes detention basins using Rational Method or SCS CN method to meet pre/post-development peak flow matching requirements
skill_spec.formula_hint: SCS method: Q = (P - 0.2*S)^2 / (P + 0.8*S) where S = 1000/CN - 10. Peak flow: qp = qu * A * Q. Storage = (post_peak - pre_peak) * duration approximation.

example_queries: Size a detention pond for a 15-acre site, pre-dev CN 65, post-dev CN 85, 6-inch design storm
What storage volume do I need if post-development runoff is 45 cfs but allowable release is 20 cfs for a 24-hour storm?

title: Construction cost estimating for bid preparation
problem: Civil engineers preparing bids and cost estimates must assemble unit costs for dozens of line items - concrete, asphalt, earthwork, utilities, drainage structures - and apply regional cost factors, mobilization percentages, and contingencies. A miscalculation or missed line item can mean losing the bid or eating a loss on the project.
who: Project engineers and estimators at consulting firms and contractors preparing bids

skill_spec.name: Civil Construction Cost Estimator
skill_spec.one_liner: Builds construction cost estimates from quantities and unit prices with mobilization, overhead, contingency, and regional adjustments

inputs.name: regional_factor
inputs.label: Regional cost adjustment factor (1.0 = national average)

skill_spec.formula_hint: Subtotal = sum(qty * unit_cost * regional_factor). Add mobilization, O&P, contingency as percentages. Provide per-item and total breakdown.

example_queries: Estimate cost for: 5,000 CY excavation at $15/CY, 2,000 tons asphalt at $95/ton, 500 LF storm pipe at $85/LF with 8% mobilization and 15% contingency
What's the total bid price with 20% overhead and profit on a $450,000 direct cost subtotal?

title: Retaining wall design and stability check
problem: Designing retaining walls requires checking sliding, overturning, and bearing capacity failures with appropriate safety factors. Engineers perform these calculations by hand or in spreadsheets for every wall segment. Missing a stability check or using wrong soil parameters risks structural failure and PE license jeopardy.
who: Geotechnical and structural engineers designing retaining walls

skill_spec.name: Retaining Wall Stability Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Checks sliding, overturning, and bearing capacity safety factors for gravity and cantilever retaining walls
skill_spec.formula_hint: Ka = tan²(45 - φ/2). Pa = 0.5 * γ * H² * Ka + q * H * Ka. FS_sliding = (W * tan(δ)) / Pa. FS_overturn = (W * x_w) / (Pa * H/3). Check bearing: q_max = (V/B)(1 + 6e/B).

example_queries: Check stability for a 10 ft cantilever wall with 120 pcf soil, 30 degree friction angle, 6 ft base width
Is my retaining wall safe? Height 8 ft, base 5 ft, soil unit weight 110 pcf, friction angle 28 degrees, 200 psf surcharge

title: PE license renewal and continuing education tracking
problem: PE license renewal requirements vary by state - different PDH/CEU requirements (typically 15-30 PDH per renewal cycle), varying cycle lengths (1-2 years), and different accepted activity types. Missing renewal deadlines means inability to practice and stamp documents, directly impacting income and firm operations.
who: All licensed Professional Engineers (PE) across all states

skill_spec.name: PE License Renewal Reference
skill_spec.one_liner: Quick lookup of state-by-state PE license renewal requirements including PDH hours, deadlines, and accepted activities
skill_spec.data_domain: State PE board renewal requirements for all 50 states and territories

data_hints.source_law: Individual state PE licensing statutes and NCEES Model Law

example_queries: What are the PE license renewal requirements for Texas?
How many PDH hours do I need in California and when is the deadline?
Which states require ethics-specific continuing education hours?

title: NPDES stormwater permit compliance checklist
problem: Construction sites over 1 acre require NPDES stormwater permits with specific BMPs, inspection schedules, and documentation. Missing a BMP installation or inspection triggers EPA enforcement actions with fines up to $64,618 per day per violation. Engineers managing multiple sites struggle to keep all compliance items on track.
who: Civil engineers and construction managers overseeing sites requiring NPDES permits

skill_spec.name: NPDES Construction Stormwater Compliance Checklist
skill_spec.one_liner: Step-by-step compliance checklist for NPDES Construction General Permit including SWPPP, BMPs, inspections, and reporting
steps: Step 1: Verify SWPPP is prepared and on-site before land disturbance begins
Step 2: Submit Notice of Intent (NOI) to EPA or state agency at least 14 days before construction
Step 3: Install perimeter sediment controls (silt fence, inlet protection) before grading
Step 4: Implement erosion controls (stabilized construction entrance, dust control)
Step 5: Conduct site inspections every 7 days AND within 24 hours of 0.25-inch rain events
Step 6: Document all inspections on standardized forms with date, inspector, findings, corrective actions
Step 7: Maintain and repair BMPs within 24 hours of identified deficiency
Step 8: Update SWPPP whenever site conditions change or BMPs are modified
Step 9: Stabilize disturbed areas within 14 days of final grading
Step 10: Submit Notice of Termination (NOT) after final stabilization achieved
warnings: Warning: Fines up to $64,618 per day per violation (2026 adjusted)
Warning: SWPPP must be accessible on-site at all times during construction
Warning: Some states have stricter requirements than federal CGP - check state-specific permit
Warning: Concrete washout must have dedicated containment area

example_queries: What are the NPDES stormwater inspection requirements for my construction site?
Give me the full compliance checklist for a construction stormwater permit
When do I need to submit the Notice of Termination for my NPDES permit?

title: Construction site inspection report generation
problem: Engineers conduct site inspections weekly or more frequently and must document observations, deficiencies, photos, and corrective actions in formal reports. Writing these reports is repetitive and time-consuming - 1-2 hours per report - but they are legally required documentation that can be subpoenaed in disputes or regulatory actions.
who: Field engineers and construction inspectors doing regular site visits

skill_spec.name: Construction Inspection Report Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates a professional construction site inspection report from field notes including observations, deficiencies, and required corrective actions
skill_spec.structure_hint: Header (project info, date, weather) -> Work in Progress -> Observations -> Deficiencies Table (item, location, severity, corrective action, deadline) -> Photos placeholder -> Conformance Statement -> Inspector Signature Block

example_queries: Generate an inspection report for the Elm Street widening project, inspected today, found rebar spacing non-conforming in the retaining wall footing
Create a site inspection report noting concrete pour observed, compaction test results pending, and erosion control BMPs need repair

title: Building code and design standard quick reference
problem: Civil engineers constantly need to look up specific provisions across multiple codes - IBC for building requirements, ASCE 7 for loads, ACI 318 for concrete, AISC for steel, ADA for accessibility. Flipping through thousands of pages or searching PDFs wastes significant time and wrong code references risk plan check rejections.
who: Design engineers referencing building codes and standards during design work

skill_spec.name: Civil Engineering Code Quick Reference
skill_spec.one_liner: Quick lookup of key provisions, tables, and requirements from IBC, ASCE 7, ACI 318, AISC, and ADA standards
skill_spec.data_domain: Building codes and civil engineering design standards commonly referenced in US practice

data_hints.source_law: IBC 2021/2024, ASCE 7-22, ACI 318-19, AISC 360-22, ADA Standards

example_queries: What is the minimum live load for office buildings per ASCE 7?
What are the ACI 318 minimum concrete cover requirements for footings?
What are the ADA ramp slope requirements?

title: Concrete mix design and strength verification
problem: Engineers must verify concrete mix designs meet specification requirements and evaluate cylinder break test results against ACI 318 acceptance criteria. When test results fall below f'c, the engineer must quickly determine if the concrete is acceptable, needs coring, or requires removal - decisions with major cost and schedule impact.
who: Structural and materials engineers evaluating concrete quality on construction projects

skill_spec.name: Concrete Strength Acceptance Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Evaluates concrete cylinder break test results against ACI 318 acceptance criteria and determines pass/fail/action required

inputs.name: test_results_psi
inputs.label: Cylinder break test results (psi) - array of values

inputs.name: exposure_category
inputs.label: ACI exposure category (F0-F3, S0-S3, W0-W2, C0-C2)

outputs.name: individual_check
outputs.label: Individual test check (no result below f'c - 500 psi)

skill_spec.formula_hint: ACI 318-19 Section 26.12.3: Strength acceptable if (1) every arithmetic average of 3 consecutive tests >= f'c AND (2) no individual test falls below f'c by more than 500 psi. If fail, investigate per 26.12.4.

example_queries: My 28-day breaks came back at 3,800, 4,100, and 3,650 psi for 4,000 psi specified concrete. Does it pass?
Evaluate these cylinder results against f'c = 5,000 psi: 4,900, 4,400, 5,200, 4,850

title: QA/QC plan review checklist for drawings
problem: Before stamping and submitting engineering drawings, PEs must perform thorough QA/QC reviews checking dimensions, notes, code references, title block info, and coordination with other disciplines. Missed errors on stamped documents create professional liability exposure and costly plan check resubmittals that delay projects by weeks.
who: Senior engineers and PEs performing quality reviews before stamping/sealing documents

skill_spec.name: Engineering Drawing QA/QC Review Checklist
skill_spec.one_liner: Comprehensive quality review checklist for civil engineering drawings before PE stamp and submittal
steps: Step 1: Verify title block - project name, number, date, revision number, PE seal and signature
Step 2: Check drawing scale consistency - verify graphic scale bar matches stated scale
Step 3: Review general notes for current code references (IBC 2021, ASCE 7-22, ACI 318-19)
Step 4: Verify all dimensions are shown, consistent, and close properly
Step 5: Check coordinate system and datum references match survey and geotech reports
Step 6: Verify structural details match calculations (member sizes, reinforcement, connections)
Step 7: Check grading plan - verify slopes, elevations, drainage patterns, and contour labeling
Step 8: Review utility plans for conflicts - check horizontal and vertical clearances
Step 9: Verify ADA accessibility compliance on all pedestrian facilities
Step 10: Cross-check quantities on plans against quantity takeoff/estimate
Step 11: Review specification references on drawings match project manual
Step 12: Confirm all sheets are cross-referenced and detail callouts match detail sheets
warnings: Warning: PE stamp on documents creates personal legal liability for accuracy
Warning: Code references must be current - outdated code citations cause plan check rejections
Warning: CAD layers from imported files may contain hidden elements - plot check required
regulatory_refs: State PE board rules of professional conduct

example_queries: Give me the QA/QC checklist for reviewing civil drawings before I stamp them
What should I check before sealing a set of site development plans?
Provide a quality control review checklist for structural drawings

title: Responding to plan check comments from building departments
problem: After submitting plans, engineers receive comment letters from building departments and plan reviewers citing code sections that need to be addressed. Crafting formal responses requires referencing the correct code sections, explaining compliance, and noting drawing revisions. Poor responses lead to multiple review cycles, each adding 2-4 weeks to the permit timeline.
who: Project engineers responding to municipal plan review comments

skill_spec.name: Plan Check Response Letter Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates a formal response letter to building department plan review comments with code references and drawing revision notes

variables.name: responses
variables.label: Response to each comment with code references

variables.name: engineer_name
variables.label: Responding engineer name and PE number

skill_spec.structure_hint: Header (project info, permit number) -> Reference to comment letter -> Numbered comment-response table (Comment # | Reviewer Comment | Response | Revised Sheet) -> Summary of revisions -> PE signature block

example_queries: Help me draft a response to plan check comments - reviewer wants ASCE 7 wind speed basis and ADA ramp compliance shown on sheet C-3
Generate a plan review response letter for 5 comments on the Maple Avenue project, permit #2026-1234

title: Project delay and liquidated damages risk assessment
problem: When construction projects fall behind schedule, engineers and project managers need to quickly assess exposure to liquidated damages, evaluate whether delays are excusable, and determine if time extensions are warranted. Mishandling delay claims can cost the firm tens of thousands in LD penalties or lost client trust.
who: Project managers and engineers managing construction schedules and change orders

skill_spec.name: Construction Delay & Liquidated Damages Advisor
skill_spec.one_liner: Analyzes construction delays to determine excusability, time extension eligibility, and liquidated damages exposure
skill_spec.expertise_area: Construction schedule delay analysis and liquidated damages assessment
decision_criteria: delay cause (weather, owner change, contractor issue, force majeure)

example_queries: We're 15 days behind on a DOT project with $2,500/day liquidated damages. Rain caused 8 days of delay. What's our exposure?
Is a design change by the owner grounds for a time extension under an AIA A201 contract?
How do I document an excusable delay claim for weather on a public works project?
